content.title: About
content.content: Cotija is a Mexican hard cheese made from cow's milk. It has a dry, crumbly texture and a salty, slightly tangy flavor, similar to Parmesan. It is commonly used to sprinkle over dishes, adding texture and a savory punch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cotija is traditionally produced in the Mexican states of Michoacán and Oaxaca.
The cheese is often called “Mexican Parmesan” because of its similar texture and culinary uses.
Typical aging ranges from 2 to 6 months, after which the cheese is grated into fine crumbs.
In Mexico, cotija is frequently served with tacos, beans, salads, and soups.
The cheese is high in calcium and protein but relatively low in fat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cotija provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium contributes to strong bones and teeth and supports nerve function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The cheese contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in lactose
items.content: Fermentation reduces lactose content, making it more tolerable for people with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Heart‑healthy minerals
items.content: Phosphorus and magnesium in cotija help maintain normal cardiovascular function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein or whey should avoid cotija.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The cheese is salty; those monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Large servings can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: While moderate, people with high cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grate cotija over tacos, chili, soups, salads, or casseroles. It also works well as a topping for burrito fillings or as a crunchy garnish for vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cheese in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. For longer storage (over 2‑3 months) it can be frozen after cutting into portion‑size pieces.
